correctness.rationale: For spider arms of edge lengths ell_i>=3, b>=3 and r>=max ell_i, deletion of hub is a full simplex. Its hub link has a contractible invariant part where at least one of N=sum(ell_i-1) interior vertices is missing. Terminal-leaf toggle in the first such arm is an acyclic fiber matching; the all-interior fiber has subsets of b tips of size at most t=r-N-1 and exactly binom(b-1,t) top critical faces in nontrivial range. Suspension proves a wedge in dimension r-1, with contractibility outside 0<=t<=b-1. Relative integral boundary on full interior faces is contraction by the sum functional on leaf exterior powers; top kernel equals wedge^t U_Z and interior orientation gives det(Z^J), establishing free integral G-module, not just mod-two Betti numbers. Independent direct graph-complex GF(2) homology covered 25 parameter cases on <=12 vertices with no mismatch. Finite checks corroborate universal proof; no equivariant wedge equivalence claimed.
